sections.heading: C — Adapting speed to road, traffic and visibility conditions
sections.markdown:
## C — Adapting speed to road, traffic and visibility conditions

FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A01
Higher speed increases the distance needed to turn, slow down or stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A01
Reduce speed before a sharp bend and when the surface is slippery or holds standing water. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A01
Tire grip depends on both tire type and condition and road-surface type and condition. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A01
Keep tires sound and properly inflated; consult the vehicle’s manual for the correct pressure. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A01
On dirt or gravel, reduce speed because grip is poorer, stopping takes longer and turning skids are easier than on asphalt or concrete. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A01
Slow before entering a curve; braking while curving can cause a skid. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A01
Reduce speed when rain, snow or sleet first begins because tire grip decreases. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends lowering speed by about 10 mph on wet pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A01
For packed snow, the handbook recommends reducing speed to half. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends snow tires or chains when snow covers the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A01
On ice, the handbook advises crawling slowly and avoiding the trip if possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A01
Studded-tire permission varies by area and road because the studs can damage pavement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A01
Cold, wet shaded areas can freeze before other places and remain icy longer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A01
Bridge and overpass pavement can be icy while surrounding roads are clear because it lacks insulating earth underneath. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A01
Near freezing, wet ice can be more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A01
At the start of hot-weather rain, surfaced oil can make pavement especially slick until rain washes it away. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A01
The manual says most tires retain good wet-road grip to about 35 mph; rising speed can make tires ride on water, called hydroplaning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A01
In heavy rain, the handbook says tires may lose all road grip at roughly 50 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A02
Bald or heavily worn tires can lose grip at considerably lower speeds than the preceding wet-road examples. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A02
To reduce hydroplaning risk, slow down during rain or on a wet road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A02
If tires seem to lose road grip, gradually release the accelerator. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A02
After traction loss, hold the wheel straight; turn only for an emergency and then do so slowly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A02
After traction loss, avoid trying to brake or turn until grip returns, subject to the stated emergency-turn qualification. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A03
With good tires, good brakes and dry pavement, reacting and stopping at 50 mph can require about 400 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A03
With good tires, good brakes and dry pavement, stopping from 30 mph can require about 200 feet. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A03
Seeing less than 400 feet ahead may make 50 mph unsafe; seeing less than 200 feet ahead may make 30 mph unsafe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A03
At night, travel slowly enough to stop inside the area illuminated by your headlights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A04
The manual estimates about 400 feet of headlight visibility and gives about 50 mph as its stopping-within-that-distance example. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A04
In very heavy rain, a snowstorm or dense fog, visibility may be only about 200 feet; the handbook says not to exceed 30 mph when unable to see farther. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A04
If a downpour prevents adequate visibility for driving, leave the road at a safe place and wait for improvement. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A04
Approach a hillcrest or blind curve at a speed that lets you stop for an unseen obstruction. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A04
Allow as much room as possible beside parked vehicles because people may step out or emerge between them. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A04
For the four-second sight-distance check, choose the farthest stationary object you can see clearly and count four seconds toward it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A04
If you reach that sight-distance marker before finishing four seconds, reduce speed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A04
Use the four-second sight-distance check at night to avoid driving beyond useful headlight visibility. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0026]

Misconceptions: the manual’s numerical examples do not guarantee a safe speed or stopping distance in every condition.
Mnemonics: less grip or less sight means less speed.
Glossary: hydroplaning means tires riding on roadway water; sight distance is the road ahead that is visible.
Dynamic facts: actual visibility, tire condition, road grip, posted speed and tire-equipment permissions need current checking.

sections.domain: Adapting speed to road, traffic and visibility conditions
sections.heading: C2 — Adapting speed to road, traffic and visibility conditions
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Adapting speed to road, traffic and visibility conditions

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Watch roadway edges and animal-crossing signs for wildlife; slow down after seeing struck animals because the area may be a crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
The manual lists deer, elk, pronghorn antelope, black bears and cougars among large-animal road hazards in New Mexico. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
The source places large game, especially deer, statewide; elk mainly in the western three-quarters, antelope in eastern/open plains and bears or cougars in mountains. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
Be especially alert for wildlife around dawn, dusk and the early hours of darkness. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A01
Do not assume an animal will move away; after one animal crosses, expect others. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A01
Hoofed animals may slow on slick surfaces, so prepare to slow and let them cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A01
Traveling faster than surrounding traffic creates repeated passing exposure; reduce speed to keep pace. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A01
Driving far slower than surrounding traffic can cause bunching and passing; if a queue forms behind you, pull over when safe to let it pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A01
When merging, try to match traffic speed and use the entry ramp to accelerate before joining the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A01
Avoid reaching the ramp’s end and stopping because you lose acceleration room and may surprise drivers behind. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A02
If waiting for a merge gap is necessary, slow on the ramp while preserving room to accelerate before joining. [A01] [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A02
Maintain traffic speed on the main roadway and move onto the exit ramp before reducing speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A02
For a turn from a fast two-lane road with following traffic, avoid slowing too early; tap the brakes and reduce speed promptly but safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A02
Spot slow vehicles early enough to change lanes or reduce speed without a sudden slowdown. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A02
Large trucks and small low-powered cars may lose speed on steep grades and need longer to accelerate into traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A02
The handbook describes tractors, animal-drawn vehicles and road-maintenance vehicles as usually traveling 25 mph or less and displaying an orange triangular slow-vehicle decal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A02
Where traffic or people crowd the available maneuvering space, reduce speed to allow response time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A02
Busy shopping areas, parking lots, downtown streets and rush-hour traffic can require a slower speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A02
Narrow bridges and tunnels bring opposing vehicles closer together and may require slowing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A02
At toll plazas, anticipate lane changes, stops, acceleration and changing lane counts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A02
Near schools, playgrounds and homes, watch for children entering the street without looking. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A02
At railroad crossings, verify no train is coming and enough space exists to clear the crossing; slow for a rough crossing surface. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0025]
